sheet.summary: Popular legend holds that British authorities sawed open two musical pillars at the Vittala Temple to find the secret hollow mechanism producing the seven notes of Sa-Re-Ga-Ma, only to find solid rock. Modern non-destructive acoustic testing revealed that all 56 pillars are solid monolithic granite whose dimensions produce resonant flexural vibrations resembling bell chimes rather than hollow acoustics. Experts disagree over whether medieval sculptors intentionally engineered these columns to match a musical scale or if the tones are an accidental byproduct of carving slender, uniform stone supports. What remains unknown is whether these ringing lithophones played an active role in liturgical music and dance rituals or why no surviving Vijayanagara manuals explain their construction technique.
